summary: Iteration 5 — Privacy Phase 1 (tracker compatibility, read-only scan). Backend fully passes (10/10 pytest). Admin UI on /livre/settings works as spec: card present, 4 counters (full=10, partial=0, none=2, unknown=6, sum=18), 10 Teltonika full rows + 2 smartphone none rows + 6 mock unknown rows, badge colors correct (emerald / rose / slate), recommended command 'setparam 1004:0 (sleep mode)' for full and '—' for unknown. STATIC AST check confirms privacy_scan.py imports no command-sending function. ONE FUNCTIONAL BUG FOUND: driver chauffeur@logitrak.ch can reach /livre/settings AND privacy-compat-card is rendered (backend correctly returns 403, but frontend does not hide the card nor restrict the route).

ui_bugs.issue: Driver role can navigate to /livre/settings and the privacy-compat-card is rendered (with '—' counters and an 'Échec du scan' toast). Spec requires either the route to be inaccessible OR the card to be absent for drivers.

integration_issues.issue: useEffect calls GET /livre/privacy/tracker-compatibility which 403s for drivers — error swallowed by toast, no graceful hide of card.

issues: React console warning 'Encountered two children with the same key' appears on login/dashboard load — unrelated to iter5 but worth tracking.

action_items: Hide <PrivacyCompatCard /> in SettingsPage.jsx when user.role === 'driver' (or restrict the /livre/settings route for drivers entirely). Currently the card renders for drivers and triggers a 403 + toast on mount.
Optional: investigate pre-existing 'duplicate key' React warning (not from iter5 but visible during testing).
critical_code_review_comments: privacy_scan.py is clean, focused (<90 lines), and has NO outbound command imports — Phase 1 invariant respected (verified by AST static check).
routes.py @router.get('/privacy/tracker-compatibility') and /{vehicle_id} are correctly gated by require_roles('admin','manager'). Backend access control is bulletproof.

Frontend access control missing: SettingsPage.jsx renders <PrivacyCompatCard /> unconditionally — should be wrapped with a role check (user.role === 'admin' || user.role === 'manager'), matching backend gating.

Wider concern: SettingsPage.jsx itself is reachable to drivers (URL /livre/settings is not protected at route level). Most edit controls inside the page already check canEdit, but new cards must follow the same pattern.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% — admin flow fully OK, driver access-control bug found

seed_data_creation: None — used existing seeded fleet (10 Teltonika full, 2 smartphones none, 6 mock unknown).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 5 backend is solid (10 pytest pass at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5.py). After main agent fixes the driver-can-see-PrivacyCompatCard bug, re-run only the frontend driver-access portion of the playwright script (login as chauffeur@logitrak.ch → navigate to /livre/settings → assert privacy-compat-card NOT present and no console errors).
rca of the issue: Backend role check is correct (require_roles('admin','manager') → 403 for drivers). Frontend SettingsPage.jsx renders <PrivacyCompatCard /> unconditionally (line 310). PrivacyCompatCard's useEffect immediately calls GET /livre/privacy/tracker-compatibility on mount; the request 403s, the catch block fires toast.error('Échec du scan de compatibilité'), and the card stays in the DOM with '—' counters. Fix: in SettingsPage.jsx wrap the component with {(user?.role === 'admin' || user?.role === 'manager') && <PrivacyCompatCard />}, OR add a route guard for /livre/settings that blocks role='driver'.
